Charity ride · Tucson, Arizona · since 1983

El Tour de Tucson

Saturday, November 21, 2026

The 43rd El Tour de Tucson is Saturday, November 21, 2026. Packet pickup and the expo are at the Tucson Convention Center in the days before.

What is the El Tour de Tucson?

El Tour de Tucson is a timed charity ride held in Tucson, Arizona, on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, with 102-, 62- and 32-mile routes that all start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center. It began in 1983 with fewer than 200 riders and now draws about 10,000 a year. Perimeter Bicycling, the nonprofit that runs it, says the ride has helped raise more than $138 million for charities since it started. The 2026 edition is November 21.

Sign up for El Tour Official site (eltourdetucson.org)

Registration opens roughly a year out and prices rise monthly: $125 through April 30, $135–$175 May through September, $185–$300 in October and November (2026 adult pricing). Riders 17 and under are free. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable; distance changes are free until October 18, then $25. The event does not run a lottery.

How the El Tour de Tucson started

Richard J. DeBernardis started the first Perimeter bicycling event in Tucson in 1983, after riding 2,218 miles from Alaska to Mexico in 40 days. That first ride had fewer than 200 cyclists and raised $4,500. A second event followed in 1986, and Perimeter Bicycling Association of America was formed around it.

El Tour became the flagship. The organizer describes it as the largest cycling fundraiser in America, with more than 311,000 riders across all Perimeter events over the years. In 2019 the charities riding with the event passed $100 million raised in total; by 2025 the figure was over $138 million. The 2026 ride is the 43rd.

The event now supports more than 120 nonprofits a year through fundraising teams. Riders can enter on their own or through a charity team at a reduced fee.

What to expect on the day

All routes start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center downtown. The century leaves at 7:00 am, the metric at 9:00 am and the 32-miler at 10:00 am. Timing is by chip on your bib and a second tag on the seatpost; your clock starts when you roll across the start line. Experienced pack riders on the 102 and 62 can apply for a Platinum corral.

Aid stations come roughly every 7–12 miles. The route closes at 4:30 pm, and aid stations shut down on a schedule that lets riders finish by then; there is no support or recorded time after that. Every finisher gets a medallion. CPSC-approved helmets are mandatory, aerobars are not allowed, and pedal-assist e-bikes ride in their own category without awards.

The century heads out past Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, along Old Spanish Trail with saguaro views near Colossal Cave, then swings south through Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley before coming back into the city. Expect a cool start and a warm, dry afternoon.

Weather in Tucson for the El Tour de Tucson

Late November in Tucson is mild and dry. Around November 20 the average daily high is about 72°F and the low about 48°F, with roughly an 8 percent chance of rain on any given day. Dress for a cold 7 am start and a warm afternoon.

The town guide

Ride, sleep, eat, fix the bike.

Tucson is the winter riding town. A 28-mile paved climb up Mount Lemmon from the desert floor to the pines; Pima County’s car-free Loop, a 54-mile circuit, more than 138 miles of path in all; dry, mild roads from October to April. The fast group ride, the Shootout, leaves University and Euclid by the university, and GABA posts a social road ride most days of the week. Fly into TUS, eight miles south of downtown. Fair Wheel Bikes rents carbon road bikes and an aluminum gravel bike, Pima Street Bicycle builds a shipped one, and The Tuxon puts bike storage in writing. El Tour de Tucson, the Saturday before Thanksgiving, is the big ride.

Fly into Tucson International (TUS), about eight miles south of downtown: Alaska, American, Delta, Southwest, Sun Country and United (Oct 2026), nonstops to about a dozen cities year-round. The Rental Car Center is a walk out the terminal’s east exit, and Uber and Lyft pick up on the first island across from baggage claim. Phoenix Sky Harbor is about 112 miles northwest up I-10, the fallback when TUS fares or routes don’t work. Groome runs a shared shuttle between the two, but nothing published says it takes a bike box. With a case, a one-way rental car down I-10 is the plain answer. Downtown is walkable and the fare-free Sun Link streetcar carries bikes between the Mercado, downtown, Fourth Avenue and the university. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shops that build a shipped bike and the rentals.

Group rides around Tucson

Free, recurring, open to anyone. Ride with locals the day before, or the week after.

  • Bicycle Ranch Saturday RoundupTucson, AZ · Every Saturday, 6:30 am. The shop’s page, dated Sept 19, 2026, says the Roundup is back after a long delay and only the faster group has run so far. Main group: about 56 miles at 18 to 22+ mph, with splits and smaller groups forming.
  • Civano Cycling Club Morning RidesTucson, AZ · Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday mornings, around when the temperature reaches 55 degrees. The time and route are posted the evening before. The page lists Thu Oct 1, 2026 at 7:00 am from Civano Blvd and Drexel Rd.
  • Cyclovia TucsonTucson, AZ · Twice a year on a Sunday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm, on car-free streets; the route changes each time. Next: Sun Oct 25, 2026, connecting South Tucson and downtown. The spring 2026 event was Sun Apr 12, through West University, Feldman’s, Sugar Hill, Keeling and Amphi.
  • GABA El Tour de Tucson Training RidesTucson, AZ · Sundays through the 11 weeks before El Tour de Tucson (week 6 is Oct 4, 2026). Meet 6:45 am, roll shortly after. Distance grows about 10% a week (66 miles in week 6).

El Tour de Tucson FAQ

When is El Tour de Tucson 2026?

Saturday, November 21, 2026. It is always the Saturday before Thanksgiving.

Where does it start?

All routes start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center downtown. The century starts at 7:00 am, the metric at 9:00 am, the 32-miler at 10:00 am.

How much does it cost?

Adult entries were $125 through April 30, 2026, rising monthly to $185–$300 in October and November. Riders 17 and under are free. Fees are non-refundable.

Is there a cutoff?

The route closes at 4:30 pm. After that there is no course support and no recorded finish time.

Can I ride an e-bike?

Pedal-assist only, no throttle. E-bikes have their own category, cannot use the Platinum corral and are not eligible for placement awards.

Where do I get my packet?

Only at the expo at the Tucson Convention Center, using the QR code from your confirmation email. A proxy can pick it up with your QR code and a photo ID.
